novelty_flags.label: thm:finite-saddle, project_justification, related_work, and literature_map
novelty_flags.one_line: The close global-effect comparator Faridani and Niehaus (2024/2026), Linear Estimation of Global Average Treatment Effects, is omitted despite deriving minimax rates jointly over experimental designs and linear estimators for the same all-treated-versus-none estimand.

soundness_flags.label: thm:remediability-classification
soundness_flags.one_line: Both claimed asymptotic iff statements follow solely by substituting the pointwise identity V_n^star=L_n from thm:finite-saddle, so this adds no independent classification content.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: For a known ANI network G, fixed contrastive effect tau, and q>=2, Proposition 2.2 states R(G,tau,q)=f_q(H) for a function of that model’s conflict graph H; Proposition 2.1 is the separate monotonicity result.

Theorem 3.1 concerns minimax testing error for nested exposure models; the paper’s abstract and Section 3 describe the worst-case Type I plus Type II error as one, rather than squared-error estimation of a causal contrast.

The paper assumes a known, including linear, exposure mapping and studies an assignment distribution plus regression/recentered-IV analysis minimizing worst-case approximate variance for spillover parameters.

The paper gives sharp partial-identification bounds and orthogonal estimation under exposure-propensity sensitivity restrictions for misspecified exposure mappings, not a chosen-design minimax RMSE saddle over a finite latent menu.

Viviano studies two-wave network-experiment design, optimizing participants and treatment assignments to minimize estimator variance under local dependence and deriving inference and variance-regret guarantees.
The paper proposes conflict-graph design and modified Horvitz--Thompson estimation for a prespecified causal effect under arbitrary neighborhood interference.

The article studies limitations of design-based causal inference and A/B testing under arbitrary and network interference, providing the nonconcentration benchmark rather than an exact finite-menu saddle.
Faridani and Niehaus study the all-treated-versus-none global average treatment effect and derive minimax rates over experimental designs and linear estimators under distance-decaying spillovers.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Add Faridani and Niehaus as the closest same-estimand design-minimax comparator, and distinguish its distance-decay and linear-estimator restrictions from the arbitrary-estimator finite-menu saddle.
Replace thm:remediability-classification with a substantive sufficient-and-necessary structural condition, or demote it to an explicit corollary of thm:finite-saddle.

Extend the n=2 nonrepresentation witness to a nondegenerate product or block family with the same mapping-wise graph multiset and a persistent risk gap, so the negative result is not only a minimal hand-built example.

recommended_next_step: Revise the literature comparison and remove or strengthen the tautological remediability theorem; the remaining exact finite-menu saddle and graph-nonrepresentation kernel is viable at field tier.
